Great resource for digital entrepreneurs, AI-curious creators, and anyone trying to navigate the online education space with clear eyes. https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/mastermindcom-vs-ai-advantage-are-tony-and-dean-selling-the-same-promise-twice #AITools #OnlineMarketing #InfoProducts #DigitalEntrepreneur #AIAdvantage
**DEV.TO:**
High-production AI webinars are starting to feel like reskinned funnels from the personal development world, and that's not a coincidence. The AI Advantage campaign uses a campaign architecture that pattern-matches almost exactly to Mastermind.com, which raises a real question about whether the automation and AI-education space is innovating its delivery or just inheriting old persuasion systems. If you build content pipelines, analyze marketing automation, or just want to understand what's underneath the polished AI-opportunity pitch, this breakdown gets into the structural layer most people skip.

---

**TUMBLR:**
there's a specific uncanny valley that lives inside certain webinars. the lighting is perfect, the promise is enormous, and something in your nervous system goes - wait, I've been here before. not this room. not these people. but this feeling. this architecture of hope with a timer at the bottom.

#ai #onlinemarketing #webinarculture #infoproducts #digitalcriticism #entrepreneurship #patternseverywhere

---

**THREADS:**
1/4
The AI Advantage webinar felt familiar the first time I watched it. Not "I've seen this person before" familiar. More like "I know exactly what's coming next" familiar. That's a strange thing to feel about something supposedly brand new.

2/4
Tony Robbins and Dean Graziosi ran Mastermind.com a few years back. Big production, big promise, urgency baked into every layer. The AI Advantage campaign has different branding, different timing, different surface-level content. But the skeleton underneath it? Almost identical.

3/4
And I kept sitting with whether that's cynical to notice. Like maybe every campaign shares DNA. Maybe all big launches rhyme. That's probably true. But there's a difference between a formula that works and a promise that gets repainted every few years for whoever the new buyer is.

4/4
The more interesting question isn't whether they're selling the same thing twice. It's whether the people buying it now are the same people who bought it then, just older and more hopeful. 2/4
